_meta.authority: Pathways — ordered uses of tools. Sits beside catalog.json (tools) and the SODOTO Skills Registry (skills). One relation each: a method REQUIRES_SKILL, USES a tool, and a tool may EMBODY a method.
_meta.sequenceLivesHere: Never on the tool. A hammer is used in many processes and does a different job in each, so a tool cannot carry order. A tool's 'used in' list is derived by scanning this file, never typed.

kinds.ontological: What is true of ethical collective action. Not performed — checked against.
kinds.diagnostic: What to do when stuck. Returns a type, a scale, and a choice of production sequence.
kinds.production: Getting a thing built, delivered and taught.
kinds.curricular: The order in which a person learns the skills. What SODOTO certifies.

_meta.confidence: DERIVED from SODOTO attestations, never typed. A Do One earns one star; a Teach One whose learner then runs it earns the second. null means not yet computed. Zero stars is a normal, publishable state.
_meta.transmissibility: From the SODOTO Skills Registry — Active, Ready or Candidate. Orthogonal to confidence: a method can be proven and untransmissible, or teachable and untested.
_meta.fallback: Where to go when lost. Not a gate — a recovery available from any depth. Marc's rule: drop back to a causal loop diagram and diagram your sentences.
_meta.stepFields: question (what you are now ready to ask), tool (the instrument), does (its job IN THIS METHOD), produces, handoff (what you carry on, and in what shape), gate (what must be true first).
_meta.statusNote: Pathway pages are drafted in docs/rcn-pathways.html but not yet built as their own pages. Confidence and transmissibility marks are proposals awaiting Marc's confirmation.

methods.name: Systemic Problem Solving
methods.problem: A neighbourhood problem keeps resisting the obvious fixes, and nobody agrees on what kind of problem it even is.
methods.context: The front door. Entered when handy heuristics have failed and before any production pathway is chosen.

steps.question: Will a rule of thumb do?
steps.does: Try the handy heuristics first. Most things are not systems problems.
steps.gate: Proceed only when the simple heuristics have actually failed. Entering the full pathway on a problem that did not need it is how these methods get a reputation for ceremony.
steps.produces: A decision to continue or stop

steps.question: What is connected to what?
steps.does: Draw the problem situation, naming the nodes AND the connections. Pen and paper first; move to the tool only once something interesting shows up.
steps.produces: Graph JSON with named nodes and named edges
steps.handoff: Everything downstream reads this graph. It is also the rung you return to from anywhere.

steps.question: What kind of problem is each part of this?
steps.does: Type each subgraph separately with Cynefin — simple, complicated, complex, chaotic, disordered. A neighbourhood problem is almost never one type throughout.
steps.handoff: The type selects the next pathway: complicated to design and engineering, complex to leverage and safe-to-fail experiments, chaotic to act-then-retype.

steps.question: When, where, why, who, how, and only then what?
steps.does: Work the Six Nested Questions in order with the people who hold the situation. Two to four hours.
steps.gate: The stakeholders must be in the room. Run alone this produces a document rather than a shared understanding, and the pathway depends on the second thing.
steps.produces: A shared, ordered account of the situation
steps.handoff: Answering What first is the standard failure — it produces solutions nobody will carry.

steps.question: Where is our power, and are we using all three kinds?
steps.does: AIC — equal time appreciating the whole, weighing stakeholders' differing valuations, and designing production and control.
steps.produces: A read on which of the three powers is available
steps.handoff: Appreciate maps to Ideals, Influence to Persons, Control to Org and Action — the governing tetrahedron's vertices.

steps.question: Would running this be beautiful, good, true and economical?
steps.does: The crown check, before committing.
steps.gate: A plan that is efficient and ugly, or effective and untrue to its ecology, fails here and does not proceed on the strength of having passed everything else.

steps.question: Which pathway now, and who has the standing to run it?
steps.does: Choose the production pathway and check the registry for whether anyone present is certified in the skills it needs.
steps.handoff: Into one of the pathways in routesTo.

methods.name: Walking the Tetrahedron
methods.problem: Everyone is working hard and nothing is coming of it. Something in the loop between people, ideals, organization and action is broken, and nobody can name which.
methods.context: The governing model used as a check. Under an hour, no facilitator required.

steps.question: Do the persons here actually aspire to the ideal?
steps.does: Test the Person to Ideal relation — Aspires to.
steps.produces: A reading on Aspiration of Persons
steps.handoff: If no, nothing downstream can be fixed by better organizing. Check whether the ideal was ever theirs or was handed to them.

steps.question: Does that ideal inspire an organization into being?
steps.does: Test Ideal to Org — Inspires.
steps.produces: A reading on Power of Inspiration of Org
steps.handoff: If no, an ideal is held privately with no standing arrangement to pursue it.

steps.question: Does the organization facilitate action?
steps.does: Test Org to Action — Facilitates.
steps.produces: A reading on Quality of Facilitation
steps.handoff: The commonest failure in practice: an organization exists, meets, and produces no action it has made easier.

steps.question: Does the action realize the originating ideal?
steps.does: Test Action to Ideal — Realizes. These four are the thick arrows: the optimum sequence is the heavy path.
steps.handoff: If no, work is happening but has drifted from what it was for. The loop never closes and people burn out without knowing why.

steps.question: Is the action teaching the organization anything?
steps.does: Test Action to Org — Teaches. Outside the optimum loop, checked last.
steps.handoff: This decides whether any of it compounds. It is SODOTO's Teach One at the scale of an institution.

steps.question: And does the whole of it come to good?
steps.does: BGTE — the second half of the crown.
steps.handoff: A tetrahedron whose four arrows all work, in service of something ugly, false or extractive, is a well-functioning machine pointed the wrong way.

methods.name: Collective Action Assessment
methods.problem: A neighbourhood holds something in common — water, road maintenance, a building, a fund — and nobody knows which parts of managing it are actually at risk.
methods.context: The WHO shelf applied to a real commons. Ostrom's model, filled in for this place.
methods.note: The only method in the set whose output is a disagreement.

steps.question: What do we actually hold in common?
steps.does: Fill the template's blank nodes with this neighbourhood's real common-pool resources.
steps.gate: The resource must be genuinely depletable AND open to access. If it is neither, this is the wrong model.
steps.produces: A named list of local CPRs

steps.question: Where is the risk, node by node?
steps.does: Colour every node — red high risk, yellow low risk, green little or none now, blue undecidable now.
steps.handoff: Blue is a legitimate answer, not a failure to answer. A model with honest blue on it beats one coloured through.

steps.question: Do our associates see the same risks?
steps.does: Have others do the exercise separately, before comparing.
steps.gate: Assessments must be made independently. This is the entire point of the method and shortcutting it removes the finding.

steps.question: Where do we disagree — especially green versus red on the same node?
steps.does: Discuss the differences over printed copies on a surface.
steps.handoff: A green-red split on one variable means two people are living in different systems. No single assessment could produce this.

steps.question: Which stage are we failing?
steps.does: Read the reds by Ostrom stage — Origin (forming), Performance (managing), Survival (surviving).
steps.handoff: Origin failures route to Systemic Problem Solving. Performance failures to Sofi-VSM. Survival failures mean conflict work first and everything else second.

methods.name: Shared Understanding to Experiment
methods.problem: The situation is genuinely complex — cause and effect are visible only in hindsight — and the group needs to intervene without pretending to predict.
methods.context: Entered from Systemic Problem Solving when Cynefin says complex.

steps.question: Do we see the same system?
steps.does: Climb the causal ladder in order: campfire conversation, cave drawing, then CLD.
steps.handoff: Shared only when people who disagree can point at the same picture and say where they disagree. The criterion for a cave drawing is that it is fit for finger pointing, not that it is right.

steps.question: Where would a small push do the most?
steps.does: Work the 14 leverage points — Meadows' twelve plus Time Horizon and Awareness of Place — from the top down, not the bottom up.
steps.produces: A ranked set of intervention points
steps.handoff: Parameters and numbers are the weakest places to intervene; paradigm, goals and the power to self-organize are the strongest.

steps.question: What do we think will happen?
steps.does: Find which variables are most influential given this feedback structure — not what the numbers will be.
steps.gate: The numbers question. Do not move to simulation until you have earned it. CLDs have no numbers, and a simulation built before the feedback structure is understood is garbage dressed in numbers.
steps.produces: Systemic roles — active, reactive, critical, buffering
steps.handoff: Into a designed experiment, not a prediction.

steps.question: What actually changed?
steps.does: Run the experiment, then read the result honestly.
steps.handoff: Back into step 1 with a revised picture. A designed experiment is a way for humans to listen to systems as they communicate back to us. Without SPC a group will claim both success and failure from the same data.

methods.name: Inspiration to Implementation
methods.problem: Something needs to exist that does not, and the group is larger than a few friends — so the fifteen things a small group does intuitively must now be done on purpose.
methods.context: The long arc, months to years. The only pathway that terminates outside itself.

steps.question: What do we notice, and what might it become?
steps.does: Private — Perception, Possibility, Purpose, Passion. Sensation before language.
steps.handoff: These four are easily missed because they are not yet in words. A group that skips them builds something nobody wants.

steps.question: Who will commit, who do we bring in, what do we decide?
steps.does: Public — Promise, Political Action, Policy.
steps.gate: No program without a promise. Planning entered before anyone has committed produces plans nobody owns.
steps.handoff: Political action is repeating the first five in each other person.

steps.question: How will the work be organized and resourced?
steps.does: Planning — Program, Project, Process.
steps.handoff: Programs carry resources, projects carry sub-plans, processes create a reliable sequence.

steps.question: Does it get made, bought, delivered and kept safe?
steps.does: Production — Product, Persuade, Purchase, Provide, Protect.
steps.handoff: Protect includes maintenance, disposal, recycling and the liabilities of failure — where most well-meant neighbourhood projects quietly stop.

steps.question: What is universal here that someone else could use?
steps.does: Posterity — abstract what is general and publish it as a pattern.
steps.produces: A new pattern on the shelf
steps.handoff: This is the move from model to pattern. Posterity is not the end of this pathway — it is the input to everyone else's Systemic Problem Solving. If we do not share the recipes, innovations will not spread fast enough to matter.

methods.name: Systems Dynamics
methods.problem: A person needs to learn to model causality, in an order that builds.
methods.context: Named in the SODOTO Skills Registry. A learning progression, not a work progression — nobody runs a project in this order.

methods.name: Organizational Diagnosis
methods.problem: A person needs to learn to see whether an organization is viable.
methods.context: Named in the SODOTO Skills Registry.

methods.name: Sense-Making
methods.problem: A person needs to learn to tell what kind of situation they are in before acting.
methods.context: Named in the SODOTO Skills Registry. Note where it ends — at the two governing models. The curriculum already teaches toward the crown.

methods.name: Mapping
methods.problem: A person needs to learn to make the flows and relations of a place visible.
methods.context: Named in the SODOTO Skills Registry.

methods.name: FedWiki Civic Practice
methods.problem: A person needs to learn to keep a neighbourhood's record and pass on what it learns.
methods.context: Named in the SODOTO Skills Registry. Ends in Pattern Writing, which is how the shelf grows.

methods.name: Formal Modeling
methods.problem: A person needs to learn to specify a designed system precisely.
methods.context: Named in the SODOTO Skills Registry.
